correctness.rationale: Independently constructed the 39-coordinate count array for every ternary word at lengths 1–13. Choosing r increasing positions in n-r+1 slots and adding j to the j-th position (zero-indexed) bijects onto admissible choices with successive gaps at least two. Counts fit unsigned bytes, since the largest total by order at n=13 is binomial(11,3)=165. Sorting exact 39-byte keys gave injectivity at 3–12 and exactly 12 size-two runs at 13, four on each two-letter support. Class counts at n=13 were 1,594,311 total and 1,594,299 singletons. A letter map pushes forward deck coordinates by summation; given distinct deck mates, map differing letters to 0 and 1, and, if present, a third used letter to 2. The resulting distinct ternary mates contradict injectivity at 3–12, or support rigidity at 13. Singleton letter counts force identical support within a class; on a given two-letter support ternary enumeration shows exactly four doubletons. This also precludes larger classes. Taking exactly one representative from every class gives both codebook formulas. The degenerate length-two assertion holds because admissible indices are then singletons only.
residual_risks: The supplied C++ was not executed; its explicit short-length injectivity assertion starts at n=5, though it computes and reports n=3,4. The independent exhaustive check explicitly confirmed 27 and 81 distinct profiles at those lengths. There is no claim beyond length 13 or for exact-length-three-only decks.
